title: One of Earth's Driest Deserts Was Covered in Snow
mediaSource: Atacama Desert snow August 2026 satellite Chile rare snowfall ALMA

scenes.title: The desert suddenly turned white
scenes.narration: In August 2026, parts of the Atacama Desert, one of the driest regions on Earth, were blanketed in snow.

scenes.title: Back-to-back storms brought the snow
scenes.narration: A series of winter storms spread snow beyond the Andes and into parts of the desert that rarely see widespread snowfall.
keywords: Chile desert snow satellite before after

scenes.title: Snow reached close to the Pacific
scenes.narration: NASA satellite images showed snow stretching west from the Andes, across the hyper-arid desert, and close to the Pacific coast.

scenes.title: Major observatories had to stop
scenes.narration: Snow and strong winds forced the ALMA radio telescope array to suspend observations and place its antennas into protective survival mode.

scenes.title: Some places also saw extreme rain
scenes.narration: Parts of northern Chile received extraordinary rainfall, with one coastal location getting roughly ten times its normal annual total in only three days.

scenes.title: Even the driest places can change fast
scenes.narration: The Atacama is famous for extreme dryness, but the right atmospheric setup can transform it quickly. Satellites captured the dramatic change from brown desert to white snow.
